x: A large number faced the starter and at his signal all were well away, with Tolley, Epsom, leading and Humphris (S.L.H.) closely following. After waiting some little time they could be seen in the distance and, on reaching me, they had covered about half the way, with Tolley still leading the way.

Although finding that final part of the race very testing, Bert finished in great style, 37 secs. ahead of Humphris, of South London, who had always been prominent, thus reversing last year's positions, when Humphris was 2nd and Bert 3rd.
Humphris fifty yards in the rear. Over the second lap, however, Humphris managed to reduce the lead and upon entering the finishing field was about twenty yards behind Allum.

In the last couple of miles, however, they drew away from the opposition and eventually ran out easy winners. Arthur Allum lost the individual title to Humphris, but led his team home to another very fine win.

At the end of the second lap (this sounds like a track race!) Close (Reading), Humphris (S.L.H.) and Edwards (Navy) were leading. Ginty, our new acquisition, was fourth, closely followed by the Nichols Bros., of Surrey.
